title: From the Editor — Four Quiet Days
settingText: Saint Oren’s built beneath and around a massive exposed dark Sunforge-like structure casting broad shade over ordinary homes, tables, workshops and foot traffic. The scale is impressive; daily life remains more important than spectacle.
summary: Art-directed opening editorial splash for Sunforge Outlaw Issue 9. Entice the reader, establish the live pressure and world feeling, and preserve the story page-one reveal.

panelPlan.text: SINGLE FULL-PAGE ART-DIRECTED SPLASH. Use one cinematic illustration rather than sequential panels. Reserve a large, deliberately quiet field for the supplied editorial body copy. The illustration supports the text without depicting the next issue's reveal literally.

LETTERING LAYOUT. Treat the supplied CAPTION lines as designed editorial typography, not speech balloons: strong heading, readable body copy, generous leading and margins, and a prominent final hook line. Do not invent any additional text, logos, signage, credits or slogans.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FROM THE EDITOR

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: There are theories that survive because every answer can be made to fit them.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The Sunfields are full of strange structures. Brandon is followed by strange coincidences. Put those together long enough and eventually the world begins to look arranged.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Saint Oren’s is built in the shade of the largest thing they have seen yet.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: If the pattern means what Eva and Raina think it might, this should be an interesting stop.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The people of Saint Oren’s have other plans for their week.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: — Jeff Hines

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Star Splitter Visions

title: Saint Oren's
summary: The group reaches Saint Oren's, a settled community built directly beneath and around the largest exposed dark structure they have encountered. Daily life treats it as architecture and shade, not revelation.

panelPlan.text: A huge ribbed black structure arches over Saint Oren's, casting broad shade over homes, tables, workshops and a children's play boundary.
People hang cloth from anchor points, lean tools against the base and route foot traffic around it as ordinary geography.
Eva and Raina both look up. Brandon looks toward the meal line.
Kayla Simmons intercepts the travelers with a basin for washing hands and a practical welcome.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: If you're eating, wash first.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That thing is enormous.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: It is excellent shade. The water is over there.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I already like this place.

title: Names If You're Eating
summary: Kayla asks the travelers for their actual names only so she can keep meal portions and sleeping places straight. Every name survives the introduction unchanged.

panelPlan.text: Kayla holds a small meal board and charcoal beside the communal kitchen.
Each traveler gives a name. Nobody flinches at Brandon Mack or offers a replacement.
Eva waits after Brandon's introduction as though expecting a second beat that never comes.
Kayla points them toward chores and food rather than asking about their pasts.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: Names if you're eating.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Brandon Mack.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Eva O'Learly.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Jessie Petrescu.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Raina James.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Samuel Hayes.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: Wash your hands. Supper is in twenty minutes.

title: Under the Black Rib
summary: Saint Oren's relationship to the structure immediately complicates the travelers' category. Locals use different parts for shade, anchoring and storage without agreeing that the whole thing is one meaningful object.

panelPlan.text: Kayla walks them through the settlement while assigning sleeping space.
One family calls a vertical section 'the wall,' children call a low curve 'the black slide,' and a workshop uses another segment as a heat-resistant backing surface.
Raina asks whether locals call the entire structure a Sunforge. Kayla says travelers do more often than residents.
Eva writes that down before asking why.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Do you call all of this a Sunforge?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: Some people do. Mostly visitors.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: What do you call it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: Depends which part I am talking about.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: That answer is going to annoy the notebook.

title: Alec Damon
summary: Samuel meets Alec Damon, an elderly community member who is clearly dying but remains part of daily household life rather than isolated in ceremonial vigil.

panelPlan.text: Samuel helps carry a meal tray into a bright back room where Alec rests near an open window.
Family members move in and out with laundry, food and ordinary conversation.
Alec is tired, sharp and irritated by how carefully everyone is speaking around him.
Brandon arrives with extra water and is introduced correctly, then leaves the focus on Alec.

dialogueInline.speaker: Alec Damon
dialogueInline.text: If everybody lowers their voice again, I am going outside to die louder.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I can arrange a chair before you make it a threat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Alec Damon
dialogueInline.text: You are the preacher.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Today I am mostly carrying water.

title: Samuel Asks
summary: Samuel learns Alec's estranged daughter is nearby but refuses to enter the house. He asks the group to remain in Saint Oren's for several days rather than assuming everybody will adapt to his pastoral work.

panelPlan.text: Kayla tells Samuel that Alec's daughter has been sleeping with cousins at the settlement edge and will not cross his doorway.
Samuel finds Jessie checking the rig rather than treating the stop as automatically indefinite.
He asks for time and states why.
Eva notices that Samuel now asks before turning a community's problem into the group's route decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I need a few days here. I am asking before I decide for everybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: For what?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Alec's daughter will not come inside. He may not have many days left.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You want to fix it?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I want to see whether they will speak.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Stay as long as the conversation needs. The rig can wait.

title: Why She Won't Enter
summary: The estrangement is neither melodramatic nor trivial. Alec sold a piece of land his daughter expected to inherit and dismissed her anger as entitlement; she has stayed away since their last fight.

panelPlan.text: Kayla briefs Samuel while they carry chairs under the structure's shade.
Alec sold a small orchard parcel during a bad season to cover community debts, believing necessity gave him the right to decide alone.
His daughter believed the land belonged to a shared family future and heard his decision as proof her plans never mattered.
Samuel refuses to reduce the conflict to pride and asks whether both facts can be true.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: He sold the orchard without asking her.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Why?

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: The settlement owed grain and medicine after the bad season.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Necessary does not always mean harmless.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: Try telling Alec that before breakfast.

title: Day Two: Cards
summary: A second uneventful day reveals something less mysterious about Brandon: he is genuinely bad at cards and dislikes losing more than his reserve suggests.

panelPlan.text: At a shaded card table, Brandon loses a small pile of coins to three Saint Oren's regulars.
He studies the cards as though they personally betrayed him.
Eva watches from nearby, delighted by a weakness that has nothing to do with false identities.
Jessie joins specifically to watch him lose another hand.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: I thought you'd be good at cards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Why?

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: You watch everybody.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Apparently not the cards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: The cards are poorly designed.

title: Alec Outside
summary: Brandon helps Alec spend part of the afternoon outside beneath the black rib. Their conversation stays with ordinary regret rather than turning Alec into commentary on Brandon's mystery.

panelPlan.text: Brandon and Samuel carry Alec's chair outside carefully, following Alec's impatient instructions.
Alec settles beneath the broad shade and watches people work.
He admits he still thinks selling the orchard was necessary and regrets telling his daughter her anger proved she was selfish.
Brandon says necessity and cruelty can occupy the same decision.

dialogueInline.speaker: Alec Damon
dialogueInline.text: I would sell it again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Then apologize for the part you would not repeat.

dialogueInline.speaker: Alec Damon
dialogueInline.text: You make that sound easy.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I did not say easy.

title: What Eva Is Missing
summary: Eva keeps waiting for Saint Oren's to produce a pattern event and nearly misses the ordinary person Brandon becomes when nobody is projecting a role onto him.

panelPlan.text: Eva notes another full day without recognition while watching Brandon laugh at a terrible joke from a card opponent.
Jessie asks what theory Brandon's bad temper over cards supports.
Eva admits she has been watching for strangeness so intently that ordinary behavior feels like wasted observation.
Jessie tells her ordinary behavior is exactly how they learn who Brandon is when nobody else defines him.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: You're waiting for something strange and missing how bad he is at losing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: He is a terrible loser.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Useful data.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Not for the mystery.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Maybe for the person.

title: Guest Books
summary: Raina checks years of Saint Oren's guest records for Brandon's face, names associated with him, or similar identity incidents. She finds nothing useful.

panelPlan.text: Kayla brings Raina two practical guest books used for meal counts and bed assignments.
Raina scans names, brief origin notes and dates, looking for Brannock, Diaz, Merritt, Surveyor and descriptions matching Brandon.
Eva helps without turning every dark-haired traveler into evidence.
The books contain ordinary repetitions of common names and no convincing precursor.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Nothing in four years of guest books.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: That feels statistically useful.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: It feels like bookkeeping to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Bookkeeping is often more useful than stories.

title: The Loudest Place
summary: Raina tries to reconcile Saint Oren's with her emerging Sunforge correlation. If large exposed structures amplify the identity pattern, this should be the loudest case yet. Instead there is nothing.

panelPlan.text: Raina spreads maps beneath the immense structure, marking prior communities and nearby dark remnants.
She circles Saint Oren's as the largest exposed structure they have encountered.
Eva offers possible modifiers: wrong kind, wrong orientation, wrong time.
Jessie warns that a theory that survives every non-event by adding a new exception is becoming hard to test.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: If the structure matters, this should be the loudest place we've seen.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Maybe it is the wrong kind.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: How many kinds do you get before the theory stops meaning anything?

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Fewer than I am tempted to invent.

title: One Word Too Many
summary: Kayla challenges the travelers' category directly. Saint Oren's residents do not assume every dark remnant shares one origin or function simply because travelers call them Sunforges.

panelPlan.text: Kayla overhears the theory discussion while carrying a basket and asks what exactly they mean by 'the structure.'
She identifies sections incorporated at different times and a detached piece hauled from another location generations ago.
Raina says the material and ribbed forms appear related.
Kayla says related does not mean identical in history, use or cause.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: You keep saying Sunforge like it is one thing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Same material. Similar structural forms.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: That tells me what your eyes group together.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Travelers understand breadth. People here understand depth.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: We may be flattening the categories before we even test them.

title: Day Three
summary: A third ordinary day becomes a small montage of life: work, meals, repairs, cards, Samuel's visits with Alec and Raina crossing out theories rather than adding spectacle.

panelPlan.text: Morning: Jessie helps repair a pump bracket.
Midday: Brandon loses another card hand and pays without grace.
Afternoon: Samuel sits with Alec while his daughter remains visible across the courtyard but does not enter.
Evening: Raina crosses out a line on her map rather than drawing a new one.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Day three. Still nothing about Brandon.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I object to the word nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: He lost money again.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: That recurrence is stronger than my Sunforge correlation.

title: At the Door
summary: Alec's daughter finally comes to the house but stops at the doorway. Samuel refuses to become their translator once both are physically present.

panelPlan.text: Late afternoon: Alec's daughter stands outside the open doorway while Alec sits inside where he can see her.
Samuel is positioned between them at first, then deliberately moves his chair aside.
Alec asks Samuel to explain why he sold the orchard. Samuel tells him to explain it himself.
The daughter enters one step, enough to make direct speech possible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Alec Damon
dialogueInline.text: Tell her why I did it.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: She came to hear you, not me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Daughter
dialogueInline.text: I know why you sold it. I came because you never cared what it cost me.

dialogueInline.speaker: Alec Damon
dialogueInline.text: Then come inside and tell me the rest.

title: What They Were Angry About
summary: Alec and his daughter finally speak directly. The goal is not clean reconciliation but specificity: she was angry about the unilateral decision and his contempt for her plans; he was angry that she treated the settlement's crisis as secondary to inheritance.

panelPlan.text: Samuel sits farther back while father and daughter face each other.
The daughter distinguishes losing the orchard from being told her future did not count.
Alec admits he called her selfish because he was afraid the community debt would destroy people he felt responsible for.
Neither retracts the underlying disagreement.

dialogueInline.speaker: Daughter
dialogueInline.text: You sold the land and then told me caring about it made me selfish.

dialogueInline.speaker: Alec Damon
dialogueInline.text: I was trying to keep people fed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Daughter
dialogueInline.text: You were also deciding that my plans were expendable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Alec Damon
dialogueInline.text: I did that part badly.

title: A Little
summary: The conversation gives Alec and his daughter a small amount of truth, not a sentimental restoration. She stays for the evening because she chooses to, not because the conflict vanished.

panelPlan.text: The daughter moves her chair closer but not beside Alec's.
Samuel quietly leaves the room once they no longer need him to keep speech moving.
Kayla asks in the hallway whether they made peace.
Samuel answers with the narrower result.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: Did they make peace?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: They finally said what they were angry about.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: Did it help?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: A little. That is what they had time for.

title: Alec's Last Evening
summary: Alec spends his last evening with his daughter and family. The travelers remain outside the room and let the center of the issue belong to people whose lives have nothing to do with Brandon's mystery.

panelPlan.text: Outside the house, Brandon, Eva, Jessie and Kayla eat late stew at a small table.
Through the open doorway, Alec's family is visible as ordinary silhouettes talking and sitting together; no private dialogue is supplied.
Samuel joins the outside table and discovers the stew is cold because he missed supper.
The group talks about food and tomorrow's weather rather than turning death into a mystery cue.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: You missed the stew while it was edible.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: I was occupied.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: It was not much better earlier.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: He is angry because he lost at cards before supper.

title: After Midnight
summary: Alec dies after midnight. Samuel brings the news to the others simply, and no one treats the death as evidence about the Rider, Brandon or the structure overhead.

panelPlan.text: Night beneath the huge black structure; most of Saint Oren's is dark except for the Damon house.
Samuel walks from the house to the travelers' sleeping area.
The others wake enough to understand his expression.
Raina closes the notebook in her lap without writing anything.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Alec died after midnight.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: Was his daughter with him?

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: She stayed.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then we help in the morning.

title: The Burial
summary: Saint Oren's buries Alec in a simple communal ritual. Samuel participates because the family asks him, not because his title makes him automatically central.

panelPlan.text: Morning burial at a modest grave area beyond the largest shade.
Family and community members do most of the speaking and physical work.
Samuel offers a brief closing only after Kayla gestures for him to do so.
Brandon helps fill earth afterward; Eva carries water to older mourners; Jessie repairs a loose cart wheel nearby because life continues.

dialogueInline.speaker: Kayla Simmons
dialogueInline.text: Say something short. He disliked long funerals.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Alec was difficult to love quietly. You loved him anyway. Carry the parts worth carrying.

title: Raina's Empty Page
summary: After four days, Raina's Saint Oren's page contains a conspicuous absence: no identity event, no unusual arrival, no Rider and no Cadre-like convergence despite the largest structure yet.

panelPlan.text: Raina sits beneath the black rib reviewing four days of notes.
She has recorded ordinary observations, names and local categories but no event matching her emerging correlation.
Eva asks whether an empty result counts.
Brandon passes with a tray and tells them not to turn his bad card record into a control variable.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: Largest structure. Four days. No identity event.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: No Rider either.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Then the structure is not sufficient by itself.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I was hoping the conclusion would be that I can stay somewhere four days without becoming evidence.

title: What We Learned
summary: As the group packs, Jessie inventories the ordinary things they learned about Brandon, while Samuel corrects Raina's temptation to call the entire stop quiet when Saint Oren's has just lost a person.

panelPlan.text: Kayla returns each traveler to the meal board long enough to settle what they owe in chores and supplies.
Jessie jokes about Brandon's coffee and card habits.
Raina calls the Brandon pattern quiet here.
Samuel distinguishes an uneventful mystery from an uneventful community.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: We learned Brandon hates sweet coffee, does not cheat and is awful at cards.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: The cards were awful.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: The Brandon pattern stayed quiet here.

dialogueInline.speaker: Samuel
dialogueInline.text: Alec died. Saint Oren's was not quiet.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: Brandon got four ordinary days.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: I recommend it.

title: Four Quiet Days
summary: The group leaves Saint Oren's with a genuine negative case. The largest obvious Sunforge-like structure and Brandon can coexist without the identity pattern appearing, preventing a simple causal link.

panelPlan.text: The five travelers move out together, with Raina and Samuel now fully on the same road rather than staged ahead or behind.
Eva looks back at the immense structure and closes her notebook rather than adding a speculative qualifier.
Raina leaves Saint Oren's marked as a negative case on the map.
Ahead, multiple roads begin converging toward the Rookery.

dialogueInline.speaker: Eva
dialogueInline.text: The biggest one gave us nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: Raina
dialogueInline.text: It gave us a limit on the theory.

dialogueInline.speaker: Jessie
dialogueInline.text: Limits are useful.

dialogueInline.speaker: Brandon
dialogueInline.text: So was supper.

title: Next: THE ROOKERY
settingText: The Rookery crossroads near sunset, many roads and many unrelated travelers converging naturally. The composition should encourage the eye to invent connections without confirming any.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: The biggest Sunforge yet gave them four days of absolutely nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: That is data too.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Unfortunately, the next stop is the Rookery.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Roads cross there.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: Travelers collect there.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: And depending on how badly you want a pattern, almost anybody can start looking like evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: NEXT: THE ROOKERY
